classification.illumination_scope: letters only; monument body and planter unlit

knowledge.plain_language_summary: A low, wide, double-sided board-formed concrete monument with a CMU block core, carrying halo-lit reverse-pan aluminum channel letters (a logo and a primary line) that glow warm white against the concrete at night. A brushed anodized secondary line is pin-mounted to a Corten weathering-steel-clad planter at the base. The concrete is board-formed to match existing site concrete and finished the same front and back.
knowledge.rationale: Board-formed concrete plus a Corten planter roots the sign in a rugged outdoor-resort material language, while halo-lit reverse-pan letters keep the night read soft and architectural rather than a bright cabinet face.
knowledge.tradeoffs: Cast concrete and weathering steel give a permanent, site-rooted, high-end read but are heavy, costly, and require the concrete to be pre-wired and engineered; halo-only lighting is subtle but lower-impact at distance than a lit face.
knowledge.when_to_use: Resort, camp, or outdoor-hospitality entries wanting a permanent, material-driven monument that belongs to a rugged natural setting.

rules_observations: Halo-only letters keep one quiet primary read and a deliberate night state distinct from the unlit concrete body.
Double-sided with the backside finished to match means both approaches are designed, not one-sided.
craft_observations: Board-formed concrete matched to existing site concrete is a strong site-fit move; the form-board texture is the finish, not a cover-up.
Corten planter and brushed anodized letters extend a restrained rugged material palette (concrete, weathering steel, raw aluminum) rather than adding color.
Remote power in a watertight back box keeps the faces and field clean of visible hardware.

aesthetic_notes.note: Reads as a permanent built landform element appropriate to an outdoor resort, not a applied pole sign; material honesty carries the design.
